quest.title: As Though Morning Dew
quest.description: The puppet has given up his original name. Just as the title "Wanderer" suggests, he has truly become a person with no name.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x500, Primogem x60, Mora x22000, Guide to Praxis x5, An Appellative Stroke x1, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: #Welcome back, {NICKNAME}, Paimon, Balladeer.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew! It feels like we just went on a really long journey... Paimon's exhausted.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: You don't like being addressed by that name?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: It's fine. But I was just thinking, I should probably change it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You won't go by "The Balladeer" anymore?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: After learning about everything The Doctor did, there's no way I can carry on using a name connected to him.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I'm not planning on returning to the Fatui, and they wouldn't take me back anyway. Recent events will have affected a lot of people, and they might not even remember who the sixth is.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you're quitting the Fatui for good?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's call it a tactical retreat...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: It's like you said, Lesser Lord Kusanali. Everything may look futile, but it wasn't completely meaningless. At least I made a lot of people forget about me.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: But that doesn't mean your own past has disappeared.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Of course.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: And your main goal, for which you gave up everything you had... you weren't able to achieve it. I hope you can see and understand that.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Changing the world, changing the past, changing the fates of other people... These are not simple things to accomplish.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: What you were looking for is complete annihilation... But this is just a fantasy. Even if The Balladeer is removed from existence, the world will not heed your will.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...Indeed. Haha, how ridiculous.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you regret doing all that, when you've gotten so little in return?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Even if I'm completely worthless, there's nothing in the world worth regretting.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Lesser Lord Kusanali, you purposely left that information in Irminsul, didn't you?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Yes, and I took pains to make sure that you'd acquire that information naturally.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Why would you go to such lengths? You trying to win me over too?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: In all honesty, your past experiences have made you a useful asset to Sumeru and to me. Winning you over was indeed a part of my plan.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: But before that, I wanted to tell you the truth about your past. If all I wanted to do was use you, then I'd be no different from The Doctor.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...Very clever.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I guess you could say that's one of my virtues.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Utility to others is what gives me worth. So if embracing my sins is what it takes to make me useful again, so be it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Nahida doesn't see you in that way.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Oh right, I almost forgot... you're the good guys. You're into justice and all that.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Sorry if I have a slightly different perspective on things. But, I don't feel like I've been duped. The wisest leaders are fated to end up with the best helpers... I can live with that.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I'm glad that you're able to think of it in that way.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, in the future, I'll continue to search Irminsul more deeply, and see what secrets can be uncovered.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Including the beginning of your twin's journey recorded in Irminsul. What exactly happened before and after that point? I want to know as well.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you. Let's hope you can find some answers.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I will try.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yes?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: After I dove into the information torrents in Irminsul, why did you go to Inazuma?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Because I wanted to know what you'd changed.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...So that's how you found out whose fate had changed, and how.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Well, whatever your reasons, you did me a favor, and I'll do everything I can to pay it back.

choices.text: ...I didn't do all of this for a reward.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Borrowing and returning are the only real relationships between individuals. I'll balance the books one day, don't you worry.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: That's not true. A relationship between two people is not simply a ledger that can be reset to zero.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I think, deep down, you realize this. People who show up in your life don't just evaporate like water drops and leave nothing behind. There is no such thing as "balancing the books."

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Some things in this world can never be brought back, and they can never be changed, which is why there is emotion in the human world.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Everything that you feel is real and lasting, and whatever is missing in you will not be made whole.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: To be human is to live with imperfections. You can choose whether or not you want to be human.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: But humans can't live without a heart, can they? Anyway, I gave up trying to become a human a long time ago.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: You understand what pain is perfectly well, even without a heart. You're just burying your feelings.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: The past is set in stone, but you can keep moving on. And the longer your future lasts, the shorter your past will become, until one day it is but a tiny fraction of your life.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: It sounds like you've got a future planned out for me.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I hope you can give Nahida a chance.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Everything's ended up being pretty darn complicated, Paimon doesn't even know where to start... But the most important thing now is that you need to follow Nahida. Otherwise, all our efforts will have been for nothing!

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: ...Then I guess I'll be helping you from behind the scenes from now on.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I'm glad that you've accepted our proposal. Why don't you choose a new name to celebrate?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, ooh, ooh! Paimon wants to pick an ugly nickname for you too!

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Why?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Because... because Paimon still doesn't like you that much!

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Hmph. Then I hope we don't see much of each other in the future.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: "A name is life's first gift." You didn't say it out loud, but I know that's what you're thinking.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: #{NICKNAME} and Paimon have helped you a lot. If you can't decide on a new name, maybe you can ask them for ideas.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Huh? You want us to decide?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nope, Paimon only does nicknames! If it's a serious name you're after... it's all yours!

choices.text: Please don't make it sound like I'm extorting you.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: There, now you have a name of your own.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: What about a nickname? Are you done yet?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, uhhh... still thinking... Stop rushing me...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Take your time. I don't need to see you again until you've thought of one.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What do you plan to do next?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Everyone who manipulated me and made me suffer will have to pay the price.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You mean, the Fatui?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: The Doctor, at least.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Now that your stance has changed, I believe your future path will change accordingly, but it won't be immediate... You still need some time to compose yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: One more thing.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: There are still some descendants of the Raiden Gokaden living in Inazuma. Some of them know... Well, they ought to know about the connection between the Raiden Gokaden and myself.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I don't plan to leave Sumeru for the time being. If you see them in Inazuma, please tell them that I was the one responsible for the Raiden Gokaden's downfall.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...Even though the events have been erased from the world, they still deserve to know the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I see... That is up to you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? But if we do that, then...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: It's fine. Let them stab their blades into my chest if they so desire. ...Maybe that's how it always should have been.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: What's that look for? Don't make that face, I know what I'm doing.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: ...That day will come.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Alright, we're done here.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Goodbye, wise deity, and you two.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He's gone...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: What he went through today would have been like living an entire lifetime in an instant. He'll need some time to calm down.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, true. But even so, after everything that's happened, he doesn't seem quite as fierce anymore.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: There were some bumps along the way, but it's all over now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So can we finally go eat? Paimon is starving!

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Thank you both. I hope you will find somewhere nice to go and relax for a while.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Hehe, no nonsense. I like it.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: ...Alright, let's call it a day.

talks.objective: Listen in on the scholars' conversation

dialogues.speaker: Sawada
dialogues.text: I've got it! I can end my novel with some words from Mikoshi Nagamasa.

dialogues.speaker: Aqaba
dialogues.text: You mean because everyone else in the story is dead?

dialogues.speaker: Sawada
dialogues.text: Yeah. I heard that Mikoshi Nagamasa died at a ripe old age. He's the perfect fit to be the narrator of the epilogue.

dialogues.speaker: Sawada
dialogues.text: "The dark clouds had dissipated, but they continued to cast their shadow in Mikoshi Nagamasa's mind for decades to come."

dialogues.speaker: Sawada
dialogues.text: "Then one night as an old man, he had a dream. On the night when that prized blade, the Daitatara Nagamasa, was forged, the people rejoiced, and there was painting, dancing, and drinking."

dialogues.speaker: Sawada
dialogues.text: "...All these expressions of joy melted down in the furnace fire and turned into red clouds that rallied around the final sunrise that Mikoshi Nagamasa saw in his lifetime."

dialogues.speaker: Sawada
dialogues.text: "Life is a story too long to be told, a journey that you must walk to behold."

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...Hmph.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew! It's about time we had a break!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: As soon as you stop, all the tiredness and hunger comes rushing back...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow! Great!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Huh? Look at that vase...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...What about it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Did someone break it while they were cleaning the room or something? But Paimon doesn't remember there being a cleaner...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (That night we stayed here, Paimon bumped into the table after being startled by something to do with The Balladeer and broke the vase.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (But The Balladeer erased his existence. He changed the world... So why is this vase still broken?)
You sound lost and confused.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Who's that?
I know why you are troubled. Any who knew of this would find their mind overwhelmed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Is there someone here talking to us?
Unfortunately, the fate of Teyvat cannot easily be changed. Perhaps a god may have a slim chance, but for anyone else... who can say.
When a small animal runs into a tree trunk, though the tree may sway, it is not displaced. The same is true of fate.
Like a vase that falls to the ground. Whether it is broken by a cat or by a bird, the result is still a broken vase, is it not?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wh—Who are you!? How do you know about all this?
History does not change easily, but human hearts can. Believe your own eyes. Only that which you see is true. What is unseen is but an illusion.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The voice has disappeared...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And who the heck was that!? And what were they doing, coming out of nowhere and saying all of that scary stuff...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Believe my eyes? Does she mean... I should trust my memories?)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh. Anyway, that vase is still lying there broken on the ground. Should Paimon go get someone to clean it up?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Feels wrong just leaving it there. Just a moment, Paimon'll be right back!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (I wonder what else awaits me in the future?)

choices.text: I'll buy some delicious treats as a reward.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Have you got anything?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: (UI)

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: You can't be serious.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hmm, let me give it some more thought.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Okay.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Is this supposed to be your attempt at a joke?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...Hmph. I have no need for these names anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yes. I think this will do.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...Ah, alright, if you say so.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: That won't work.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...This is a bad idea.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: You want to share your name with me? Huh, not a bad choice.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Are you sure?

dialogues.speaker: Sawada
dialogues.text: Aqaba, thanks for inviting me to research together!

dialogues.speaker: Aqaba
dialogues.text: Of course, Sawada. Your creativity has been indispensable to me. Without you, I'd have scratched my head bald by now.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Thank you so much. Please get some good rest, you must be exhausted. You know, take a shower, take a dook-dook... you'll feel as good as new.

dialogues.speaker: Sawada
dialogues.text: (I guess the sword that entered Mikoshi Nagamasa's memory in his final moments was called Daitatara Nagamasa instead of Katsuragikiri Nagamasa because he still had fond memories of it.)

dialogues.speaker: Aqaba
dialogues.text: (I feel like you've enlightened me. I can finally finish my essay! Hahaha!)

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: (It feels like... I've lived two lives.)
